title: School segregation, student performance, and school progression in Hungary
title_hu: Iskolai szegregáció, tanulói teljesítmény és iskolai továbbhaladás Magyarországon
outlet: Munkaerőpiaci Tükör 2022 — társadalmi egyenlőtlenség és mobilitás
summary_en: Hungarian schools are visibly socially segregated — but how does this segregation interact with student performance and progression? Hermann uses OKM (National Assessment) and KIR administrative-school data to quantify between-school sorting on social background and to estimate the contribution of segregation to test-score variance and to subsequent grade-progression and dropout rates. The chapter documents that segregation explains a large share of the social inequality of measured outcomes and that disadvantaged students in segregated schools have substantially worse trajectories.
policy_relevance: Direct input to Hungarian education-equity policy (BM Köznevelési Stratégia, OFI). Argues for desegregation-targeted measures — controlled school catchments, integration-bonus funding, free-school-choice constraints in segregated districts — over generic equity spending. Provides the quantitative baseline against which OECD- and EU-level Hungarian equity benchmarks can be evaluated.
